title: Surjectivity in the local proper-flat structure-sheaf criterion
statement: Let f:X→S be proper, flat and locally of finite presentation, and let s∈S. If the canonical map on the fibre over s is an isomorphism, then the stalk map induced by the tensor pullback/direct-image adjunction unit is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0E62, proof of perfect-lemma-proper-flat-h0, localized at s

proof.text: Install the standard derived localizations. The tensor pullback is additive because it is a left adjoint. The structure sheaf is invertible and therefore finitely presented and relatively flat for the flat morphism f. Apply [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] to obtain perfectness of E = Rf_*O_X[0].

Obtain the derived lift a and its ordinary H0 comparison from [lem-sc-flat-derived-structure-unit]. The given fixed-fibre hypothesis gives invertibility of its degree-zero derived residue map; its negative fibre cohomology vanishes. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-local-degree-zero-unit] to E and a to obtain surjectivity on the H0 stalk.

Apply the abelian stalk functor to the H0 comparison square. Surjectivity of H0(a), followed by the target comparison isomorphism, gives surjectivity of the ordinary structure map. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] that map is the chosen tensor adjunction unit followed by pushforward of an isomorphism. Apply the stalk functor and cancel that isomorphism using its injectivity. This gives the desired surjectivity of the chosen unit stalk map.
